question: In the cover-uncover test, movement of the UNCOVERED eye on covering the fellow eye indicates a manifest deviation (tropia), whereas movement of the COVERED eye on uncovering indicates a latent deviation (phoria).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is FALSE. You observe the COVERED eye when you remove the cover: if it moves to take up fixation, a phoria is unmasked. Movement of the uncovered eye on covering the fellow eye reveals a tropia. The distinction is fundamental to strabismus assessment.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect — the statement has the eye movements reversed. Movement of the UNCOVERED eye when you cover the fellow eye indicates a tropia (manifest); movement of the previously COVERED eye when uncovered indicates a phoria (latent). A key distinction in EOM examination.
